lessons.task: Predict how doubling stiffness changes static displacement and ringing while mass and damping stay fixed.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Static displacement follows F/k; natural frequency follows sqrt(k/m), while damping ratio changes with both k and m. Separate integration-driven energy growth from physical forced response.
lessons.claim_limit: Linear spring and viscous damping do not model friction, yielding or nonlinear stops.

lessons.task: Distinguish a bounded first-order step response from the unbounded integral of the same constant input.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The first-order response approaches its DC gain over its time constant; an integrator accumulates area. A slower pole changes approach time rather than converting the equilibrium into a ramp.
lessons.claim_limit: Finite-time traces cannot establish a limit without the differential equation.

lessons.task: Connect visible decay and oscillation to the real and imaginary parts of the displayed poles.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A negative real part sets exponential decay; conjugate imaginary parts set angular frequency. The same endpoint can occur at different oscillation phases, so use the history and pole locations together.
lessons.claim_limit: Linear modal predictions do not establish nonlinear global stability.

lessons.task: Identify when a small-angle pendulum ceases to predict the nonlinear motion accurately.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The sine law and its tangent coincide only locally. Larger initial angles change restoring torque and period; agreement near the equilibrium is insufficient at large excursions.
lessons.claim_limit: The undriven ideal pendulum omits friction and actuator dynamics.

lessons.task: Explain how proportional gain moves response speed and residual tracking error in the actual loop.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Closing the loop changes the denominator as well as the reference response. A smaller steady error can coexist with larger transient effort, and incorrect feedback sign can destabilize the state.
lessons.claim_limit: A nominal proportional loop is not an integral servo or robust performance proof.

lessons.task: Show which PID term changes initial effort, accumulated bias and damping without tuning all gains together.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Integral action accumulates error and derivative action responds to the modeled rate. A transient improvement must be interpreted alongside actuator demand; increasing every gain obscures the causal mechanism.
lessons.claim_limit: The lab's ideal derivative is not a noise-qualified implementation.

lessons.task: Reconcile a time-response oscillation with the loop margin and actuator-lag change.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Added lag changes phase near crossover and can reduce stability margin even if low-frequency gain improves tracking. A positive gain margin alone does not summarize every crossover or delay effect.
lessons.claim_limit: Finite frequency sampling is not exhaustive robust stability certification.

lessons.task: Compare feedback disturbance rejection at zero frequency and at a higher disturbance frequency.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The closed-loop sensitivity attenuates some disturbances but its attenuation varies with frequency. Identify the disturbance injection point before equating an output change to the loop gain.
lessons.claim_limit: The modeled injection and sensor paths determine which sensitivity function applies.

lessons.task: Predict how controller sample period changes a discrete integral update and the actual closed-loop path.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Integral accumulation includes the sample interval; omitting or misapplying it changes the effective gain. Compare identical physical time spans rather than equal sample counts only.
lessons.claim_limit: A software discretization does not establish target timing or quantization performance.

lessons.task: Separate sample-and-hold delay from a fractional transport delay in the plotted response.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Time delay adds frequency-dependent phase; a fast sample rate does not remove an independent transport delay. Interpret failure using the actual delayed path instead of nominal continuous poles.
lessons.claim_limit: The retained delay model is an approximation with a fixed execution convention.

lessons.task: Determine when a requested command is feasible and trace the plant driven by its applied value.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The actuator limit bounds applied command rather than requested command. Tracking can fail despite nominally stable poles if sufficient control authority is unavailable.
lessons.claim_limit: Static clipping omits actuator rate, heating and mechanical dynamics.

lessons.task: Explain why reducing the demand after saturation does not immediately erase stored integral state.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The integrator retains its history during saturation; anti-windup feeds back the request/applied discrepancy. Recovery should compare the same demand duration and limit, not a more favorable test.
lessons.claim_limit: An anti-windup example does not guarantee every reference can be tracked.

lessons.task: Use a zero input gain or coupling limit to distinguish controllability rank from control effort.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The span of B, AB and higher powers identifies reachable directions. A barely nonzero coupling can preserve rank yet make reaching a state poorly conditioned and expensive.
lessons.claim_limit: Binary rank alone does not quantify numerical conditioning or bounded-input reachability.

lessons.task: Explain why a longer observation window cannot restore a fundamentally missing measured direction.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Observability involves C, CA and the state dynamics. Longer data may improve an existing weak direction, but identical or absent sensitivities retain a null space.
lessons.claim_limit: A nominal rank test is not noise-qualified estimation accuracy.

lessons.task: Balance observer pole speed against a fixed sensor bias and explain the actual error trace.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Stable observer error poles govern transient convergence when the model and measurement are valid. A persistent sensor bias is a forced error; faster poles do not make a biased measurement true.
lessons.claim_limit: The deterministic observer is not an optimal stochastic filter.

lessons.task: Predict what happens when assumed measurement noise disagrees with the retained noisy sensor stream.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Kalman gain balances propagated covariance against assumed measurement covariance. Smaller reported P can mean overconfidence rather than smaller actual error, so inspect innovations and truth error separately.
lessons.claim_limit: A deterministic example does not establish probabilistic confidence coverage.

lessons.task: Compare state-error and control-effort weights while recording both state history and applied control.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The LQR objective trades state cost against input cost; larger state weight generally changes gains and effort. It does not impose hard actuator constraints unless those constraints are modeled separately.
lessons.claim_limit: Nominal unconstrained LQR is not a saturation or robust guarantee.

lessons.task: Show how feedforward changes nominal tracking while feedback reacts to disturbances and mismatch.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Feedforward uses the reference and model to anticipate required effort; feedback corrects measured error. A perfect nominal trace with feedforward alone does not prove rejection of model error.
lessons.claim_limit: The feedforward model and reference smoothness bound the claim.

lessons.task: Predict the effect of actual actuator gain and drag mismatch without redesigning the nominal controller.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Model error changes the physical loop while the nominal design remains fixed. Compare gain and drag sweeps independently; a robust claim must name the tested uncertainty family and performance measure.
lessons.claim_limit: A sampled two-parameter family is not all possible plant uncertainty.

lessons.task: Choose between nominal and robust designs using their observed uncertainty/effort tradeoff.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A conservative design can sacrifice nominal speed to maintain acceptable response under a declared mismatch. Compare both at the same physical plant and include effort or tracking penalties.
lessons.claim_limit: No untested uncertainty set or universal robust certificate is implied.

lessons.task: Check whether changing distance or move duration violates the generated trajectory's limits.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Time scaling changes velocity and acceleration at different powers of duration. A geometrically smooth reference may still demand infeasible actuator authority; check each derivative with its units.
lessons.claim_limit: Reference feasibility is not guaranteed closed-loop tracking.

lessons.task: Explain the signs and dimensions of the bounded proportional-navigation teaching example.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The modeled acceleration uses a navigation constant, closing speed and line-of-sight rate. State the closing/angle conventions before interpreting a miss distance or saturation event.
lessons.claim_limit: This is a bounded synthetic guidance-method illustration, not operational system validation.

lessons.task: Trace how a sensor lag and actuator lag alter the measured and applied paths separately.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The controller acts on delayed measurement and drives a lagged actuator. Their phase and amplitude effects occur at different loop locations, so matching time constants does not make them interchangeable.
lessons.claim_limit: The linear lag model omits real sensor faults and actuator constraints beyond its scope.

lessons.task: Calculate which timing and latency assumptions the software HIL example actually exercises.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A controller period and one-way latency affect command arrival and sample age. A simulated plant loop can validate its timing model and recovery logic while leaving real buses and devices entirely untested.
lessons.claim_limit: This is software simulation, not physical HIL or a real-time scheduler measurement.

lessons.task: Compare operating-point residual and tangent-model error when changing angle and perturbation independently.
lessons.expected_reasoning: An equilibrium must first balance gravity torque. The Jacobian describes a local perturbation after that balance; a small Taylor error cannot excuse linearizing around an unbalanced state.
lessons.claim_limit: The approximation is local and excludes large-angle dynamic equivalence.

lessons.task: Distinguish equivalent state/transfer realizations from an invalid near pole-zero cancellation.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A coordinate realization preserves the full transfer relation. Dropping a nearly cancelled mode changes the model unless exact cancellation and the relevant input/output assumptions hold.
lessons.claim_limit: Input/output cancellation does not establish every internal state is harmless.

lessons.task: Relate damping and natural frequency to overshoot, settling estimates and system-type error.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Damping changes the decay envelope and ringing; natural frequency scales time. A four-time-constant rule is an estimate, and an unstable response has no legitimate settling-time certification.
lessons.claim_limit: The displayed second-order model is not a universal transient specification.

lessons.task: Select a gain from root locations rather than choosing the fastest-looking finite response.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Closed-loop roots determine nominal linear stability; a root crossing into the right half-plane invalidates a stable design claim even if a short trace is initially small.
lessons.claim_limit: Dominant-pole approximations omit non-dominant modes and actuator constraints.

lessons.task: Count open-loop unstable poles before interpreting a Nyquist winding around minus one.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The relation between winding and closed-loop unstable poles depends on the declared contour convention. Verify polynomial pole counting as a separate check; a visually small loop is insufficient.
lessons.claim_limit: A finite sampled contour can miss critical behavior, especially near imaginary-axis crossings.

lessons.task: Measure sensitivity, complementary sensitivity and effort together while shaping the loop.
lessons.expected_reasoning: For negative feedback S+T=1. Improving disturbance rejection in one frequency region can increase noise or effort elsewhere; an incorrect feedback denominator breaks the identity.
lessons.claim_limit: Peak values are over the declared sampled frequency band.

lessons.task: Explain why a lead stage adds phase while a lag stage changes low-frequency gain differently.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Lead and lag are identified by their pole-zero ordering, not a component name. Swapping the lead pole and zero reverses the phase effect; compare the same frequencies and scaling.
lessons.claim_limit: An isolated compensator plot does not certify the full closed loop.

lessons.task: Place the notch relative to the actual resonance and distinguish it from a reference prefilter.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A notch reduces loop transmission near its chosen center, while a prefilter changes reference content. Mistuning the notch can leave the physical resonance exposed even if reference motion looks smoother.
lessons.claim_limit: The fixed resonance model omits uncertainty and changing structural modes.

lessons.task: Compare static decoupling, relative gain and dynamic singular values before choosing channel pairing.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A DC inverse can reduce static cross coupling without cancelling dynamic interaction at every frequency. Regularization trades inversion sensitivity against a residual; transmission zeros constrain the attainable behavior.
lessons.claim_limit: This two-input/two-output example is not full control allocation or MIMO robust synthesis.

lessons.task: Hold both decay rates fixed and change the angle between the eigenvectors.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Eigenvalues remain stable while nearly parallel eigenvectors amplify coordinate sensitivity and transient cancellation. A tiny reconstruction error is not proof that the modal basis is well conditioned.
lessons.claim_limit: Roundoff reconstruction residual is not a physical state error bound.

lessons.task: Compare exact ZOH, Euler pole mapping and alias-equivalent sampled tones at the same sample interval.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The exact scalar pole is exp(aT), whereas Euler uses 1+aT. A stable continuous pole can map to an unstable Euler pole; sampled sinusoidal frequency is ambiguous modulo sampling frequency.
lessons.claim_limit: The retained lab compares a scalar pole and tone, not a full sampled-data loop.

lessons.task: Separate state-feedback pole placement from reference prefilter scaling in the actual two-state trajectory.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Both position and velocity terms contribute acceleration. Changing only the prefilter moves the equilibrium without moving closed-loop poles, so tracking error and pole stability are different tests.
lessons.claim_limit: A finite endpoint does not equal the analytic final value automatically.

lessons.task: Compare integral load rejection with the requested and limited command at identical authority.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Integral action can reject a feasible constant load while command saturation prevents impossible equilibria. Track the integral state as well as position; a stable unsaturated design is not enough.
lessons.claim_limit: The normalized first-order servo is not a complete second-order mechanical plant.

lessons.task: Verify controller and observer modes in the augmented system rather than looking only at controller poles.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The separation principle joins regulator and estimator modes under its assumptions. An unstable observer can spoil the actual estimated-state feedback trajectory despite stable regulator modes.
lessons.claim_limit: This nominal linear result excludes saturation and model mismatch.

lessons.task: Explain why a terminal Riccati boundary must be propagated backward in time.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The finite-horizon value at the end is prescribed. Starting that value at the beginning solves a different boundary problem; compare the terminal metric and time-varying gain schedule.
lessons.claim_limit: The lab uses a declared finite-difference Riccati scheme, not an exact continuous optimizer or full state-cost rollout.

lessons.task: Increase converter bits while keeping sampling jitter fixed and explain any error floor.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Quantization error shrinks with code spacing, but timing error depends on waveform slope and jitter. Separate the two error traces before assigning combined SNR improvement to resolution.
lessons.claim_limit: The deterministic jitter and quantizer do not model every ADC error mechanism.

lessons.task: Explain the difference between slow-rate hold error, execution delay and timestamp-derived age.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A held sample accumulates age within its rate period; transport/execution delay adds another contribution. A nominal phase-lag number alone does not prove data freshness for every tick.
lessons.claim_limit: Fixed software index timing is not measured operating-system scheduling.

lessons.task: Predict the command jump when switching from manual to automatic control and explain the recovery criterion.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Bumpless transfer initializes integral state to match the existing command. Anti-windup then uses the actual saturation discrepancy; a recovery beyond the finite observation window is censored, not an observed success.
lessons.claim_limit: A censored recovery is a lower bound on time, not an exact settling measurement.

lessons.task: Distinguish local damping stability, a phase-portrait orbit and global energy behavior.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The double-well potential has several equilibria. Reversing damping changes energy flow and local stability; distance from one well at a single oscillation phase is not a valid stability ranking.
lessons.claim_limit: A finite simulated orbit is not a global Lyapunov proof.

lessons.task: Test the selected Lyapunov sublevel using the actual vector field and its boundary derivative.
lessons.expected_reasoning: For V=x squared/2 and xdot=-x+b*x cubed, Vdot=-x squared+b*x fourth. Strict negativity requires a sublevel inside the nonzero equilibria, with the origin excluded from the strict test.
lessons.claim_limit: Equality at the boundary does not certify asymptotic convergence.

lessons.task: Compare a barrier condition evaluated along the actual state trajectory with the nominal command.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A safety filter must recompute its constraint at each evolving state. Check feasibility and realized barrier margin rather than assuming a projected command guarantees all future motion.
lessons.claim_limit: The finite sampled barrier model does not certify arbitrary continuous or delayed plants.

lessons.task: Measure gain interpolation error against the underlying schedule at an intermediate operating point.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A table and interpolation rule produce an approximation. Sparse sampling can hide error between knots; matching a few endpoint gains does not establish uniform performance over the operating range.
lessons.claim_limit: The specified schedule is not a universal gain-scheduling stability proof.

lessons.task: Explain an actual departure event when feedback cancellation uses a mismatched nonlinear model.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Cancellation leaves residual dynamics whose sign can change stability or produce finite escape. Report the event and finite validity interval rather than extending a plotted solution past departure.
lessons.claim_limit: Feedback linearization relies on the modeled input map and valid operating domain.

lessons.task: Compare worst sampled sensitivity over the declared uncertainty interval with the nominal response.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Robust performance names an uncertainty set and a performance quantity. Dimensionless normalized margins must not mix incompatible units; a sample grid is evidence for that grid, not an exact all-frequency theorem.
lessons.claim_limit: Finite grids do not establish structured singular-value certification.

lessons.task: Check applied receding-horizon commands against both optimization feasibility and actual state constraints.
lessons.expected_reasoning: MPC repeatedly solves a constrained horizon problem. A decreasing objective does not excuse an infeasible input or state, and finite horizon plus a fallback is not automatically a stability proof.
lessons.claim_limit: This bounded scalar optimizer is not a general nonlinear MPC implementation.

lessons.task: Show why rich excitation and held-out validation are separate requirements for identification.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A low fitting residual can arise from uninformative data or overfitting. Rank and excitation establish identifiability; independent free-run validation checks whether the fitted dynamics predict new behavior.
lessons.claim_limit: Noise-free low-order ARX identification does not establish real plant accuracy.

lessons.task: Relate recursive least squares estimates and covariance to an independently weighted batch fit.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Each RLS update uses a gain and covariance recursion. Forgetting changes the data weights; small covariance without sufficient excitation is not trustworthy certainty about the true parameters.
lessons.claim_limit: The retained model and excitation family limit the adaptation claim.

lessons.task: Distinguish zero-mean state prediction from covariance growth under a random walk.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Positive process noise adds qT to initial variance. The mean can remain unchanged while uncertainty grows; subtracting noise can produce an invalid covariance even if a clipped plot stays finite.
lessons.claim_limit: The experiment is scalar covariance propagation, not a general vector stochastic process.

lessons.task: Compare NIS before a gated update and NEES after it using the retained truth trajectory.
lessons.expected_reasoning: NIS divides squared innovation by S; NEES divides posterior truth error by P. Bypassing the gate changes the posterior path at the same injection; independent-trial consistency cannot be inferred from deterministic time samples.
lessons.claim_limit: NEES needs truth and deterministic samples do not validate chi-square coverage.

lessons.task: Calculate the actual EKF state update and nonlinear residual from the selected prior.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Linearize the measurement at the prior, compute innovation and gain, and update both state and covariance. A zero Jacobian loses first-order information; prior variance is not the nonlinear Taylor residual.
lessons.claim_limit: This single scalar update does not resolve the global sign ambiguity of squared observations.

lessons.task: Explain the difference between sigma-point mean weights and covariance correction for a squared Gaussian transform.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The squared zero-mean Gaussian has mean sigma squared and variance twice sigma fourth. A missing covariance correction can preserve the mean while corrupting variance; the two weight sums have different roles.
lessons.claim_limit: This is an unscented transform component, not a recursive UKF.

lessons.task: Explain why later measurements can reduce an earlier state's uncertainty in an RTS smoother.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A smoother conditions on future data through a backward gain while a filter conditions only on data available at the time. Compare full conditional covariance, not an arbitrary fixed percentage improvement.
lessons.claim_limit: The retained scalar random-walk example is not a general navigation smoother.

lessons.task: Check quaternion normalization, vector calibration and round-trip frame consistency separately.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A valid rotation preserves norm and orthogonality. Scaling quaternion components without normalization corrupts the rotation; a plausible vector endpoint alone cannot verify the full frame transformation.
lessons.claim_limit: One composed rotation does not establish full attitude-estimation accuracy.

lessons.task: Build the actual two-column calibration regressor and decide whether separate bias uncertainty is available.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Information is Y-transpose R-inverse Y. Identical columns have rank one regardless of noise scale; with diverse headings use singular values and the inverse information covariance to quantify sensitivity.
lessons.claim_limit: This normalized two-parameter geometry is not full inertial alignment.

lessons.task: Compare prescribed accelerometer-bias correction over the same coast interval and inspect plotted endpoints.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Velocity error is bias times time and position error is half bias times time squared. A five-percent residual bias produces five-percent position error; omitting correction leaves the full drift.
lessons.claim_limit: The model has fixed attitude and does not execute full strapdown navigation.

lessons.task: Separate position and clock error in a nonlinear synthetic pseudorange solution.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Each range measurement contains geometry and a common clock term. Omitting that term forces the solver to absorb timing error into position; residual size alone does not identify the error source.
lessons.claim_limit: Synthetic geometry and deterministic noise are not real GNSS qualification.

lessons.task: Trace prior covariance, state-error injection and covariance reset in the actual one-axis filter.
lessons.expected_reasoning: An error estimate must be injected into the nominal state as well as propagated in covariance. A shrinking covariance with an uncorrected nominal error is overconfidence, not successful navigation.
lessons.claim_limit: This one-axis formulation does not implement a complete inertial ESKF.

lessons.task: Compare actual residual-based detection and exclusion with the refitted solution and alarm threshold.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Redundancy permits inconsistency detection under stated geometry. Excluding a suspect row changes the fitted position and residual structure; distinguish a synthetic threshold from a certified protection level.
lessons.claim_limit: No aviation integrity or protection-level certification is supported.

lessons.task: Predict the initial LOS heading and compare nonlinear cross-track evolution with its local approximation.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The actual heading is minus atan(y/L); lateral speed is V times its sine. Exponential decay is valid only for small y/L, and reversing the sign causes growing error with a changing peak heading.
lessons.claim_limit: The lab follows a straight path with instantaneous heading tracking, not a full waypoint controller.

lessons.task: Explain the different moving-beacon guidance paths using the actual relative geometry.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Closing speed, line-of-sight rate and turning geometry govern the trajectory. Compare bounded civilian synthetic paths under the same initial conditions rather than treating a smaller endpoint distance as universal superiority.
lessons.claim_limit: These synthetic beacon comparisons do not validate an operational pursuit system.

lessons.task: Compare a bounded terminal objective with its actual optimized controls and residual.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A finite control horizon trades terminal error against limits. If the desired terminal state is infeasible, report the residual and active bounds rather than silently declaring success from solver convergence.
lessons.claim_limit: This bounded teaching problem is not a complete autonomous planner.

lessons.task: Trace excitation, identified model, redesigned controller and estimator into the held-out stress histories.
lessons.expected_reasoning: Identification rank must support both fitted coefficients. Stress changes the physical model while the design and estimator use the identified model; each requirement derives from recorded state, covariance or control evidence.
lessons.claim_limit: A scalar synthetic identification/control/estimation loop is not full vehicle dynamics or robust certification.

lessons.task: Reconcile actual survey position, estimated position, turn limits and stale-navigation hold events.
lessons.expected_reasoning: The planar survey applies LOS guidance and a bounded turn command to a simplified navigation estimate. GNSS age can trigger a hold even if cross-track error is small; inspect each requirement and the executed path.
lessons.claim_limit: The capstone uses simplified planar position aiding, not raw pseudoranges or full GNSS/INS mechanization.

lessons.task: Trace each software-HIL verdict to delivered packet timing, dropped commands and expired actuator state.
lessons.expected_reasoning: A watchdog must suppress actual applied output when a command expires. Distinguish late delivered packets from dropped source commands, and track the proportional-loop equilibrium rather than assuming unity tracking.
lessons.claim_limit: Software event simulation does not measure real buses, operating-system deadlines or physical actuators.

claim_boundary: Authored synthetic-software scope only; no learner completion, physical HIL, full strapdown/GNSS-INS, MATLAB or production acceptance.
